transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Arcadia), Marta (Arcadia Eng Mgr), Samir (Arcadia Partnerships)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
- Co-sell planning: prioritized accounts, account heatmap review, risk triage for large deals in healthcare vertical.
- Technical ask: baseline latency/cost for 1k/5k/10k token workflows; VPC/private deployment and data residency questions.
- Security: SOC2 proof, SSO/SAML, audit logs and KMS key ownership.
- Next steps: share one-pager, run benchmarks, schedule exec alignment.

Topics: account heatmap; pilot scope; hosting model tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private); SOC2 & compliance; pricing guardrails; co-sell motions and success metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. sound ok on time?
[00:06] Jordan: yeah good, thanks, appreciate it. we pulled together a quick list of the top 8 accounts we want to push through Q1.
[00:12] Maya: awesome, we'll run through the heatmap then call out where Redwood can help accelerate. Diego, quick note on the benchmark you prepared?
[00:18] Diego: sure, i have the baseline numbers but i'll summarize high level first — running on our Dedicated 4xA100-type equivalent, continuous batching on small sequences gave about 35ms p95 for 1k tokens, and for 10k-token replay it was more like 250ms per token in aggregate — there's some jitter depending on KV cache warming. those numbers are rough off demo infra, i want to run them on Arcadia samples.
[00:41] Marta: sorry can you repeat the 250ms per token? that seems high for our streaming flow.
[00:46] Diego: yeah, so that's per token when you're replaying full 10k sequences without prefix cache — we usually see amortized cost decrease significantly once caching and prefix reuse is enabled. for interactive small prompts p95 is the more relevant metric.
[01:05] Samir: from a co-sell perspective, Arcadia's biggest ask is data residency and auditability for payer integrations — so Private or Dedicated with VPC is non-negotiable for some deals.
[01:15] Maya: noted — that's consistent with other healthcare partners. quick question, Jordan, timeline for pilots and procurement?
[01:21] Jordan: aiming to start pilots by mid jan, procurement wants pricing and SOC2 evidence beforehand. also our security team will want KMS integration and to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys.
[01:33] Priya: we do support customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with common KMS options and provide audit logs. i'll share the SOC2 link and sample audit output — it lives in our trust center.
[01:46] Jordan: perfect, please send that.
[01:48] Marta: a technical nit — latency SLOs are critical for our clinician-facing flows. can you explain routing/fallbacks if a specific dedicated pool is saturated?
[01:58] Diego: yes, so the smart routing layer can fallback to a compatible model variant in another region or to hosted capacity depending on policy — there's a routing policy that prioritizes latency or cost. if you choose strict data residency, fallback is limited; we can set canary fallback policies that failover to a pinned model in the same VPC region.
[02:17] Jordan: ok but cost also matters; we don't want to blow the budget during high traffic days. what levers do we have?
[02:24] Maya: batching, prefix caching, and model quantization recommendations — Redwood Optimize will provide suggestions per workload. also Reserved Dedicated capacity with burst policies helps keep unit costs predictable.
[02:36] Samir: regarding co-sell, we want clear ROI messages — if we push these three accounts, what's the pitch vs FastServe AI?
[02:43] Maya: call that out: our differentiators are predictable cost controls, unified API across Hosted / Dedicated / Private, and first-class observability. vs FastServe they often push hosted-only and have opaque token pricing; vs CloudEndpoints they focus infra not inference optimizations. we'll share a one-pager that frames these benefits for healthcare buyers.
[02:58] Marta: about compliance — how granular are audit logs? need to show who invoked models and what prompts were used (redacted where required).
[03:07] Priya: audit logs include request metadata, route, model version, and token counts. payload retention can be configured and we support redaction and filtered retention for PHI. we'll need to align on retention windows for each account.
[03:23] Jordan: procurement will ask about SSO and SCIM for provisioning partners and cross-org pilots.
[03:28] Diego: we support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning; for Private installs we can integrate with their IdP and map RBAC roles. there may be a short configuration sprint for SCIM attribute mapping.
[03:40] Samir: what about co-sell compensation — is there a standard rebate or MDF play?
[03:44] Maya: we typically structure a co-sell discount + rebate tied to net new ARR and pilot conversion. i'll include a suggested financial split in the one-pager but final terms will go through partner ops.
[03:53] Jordan: on the pilot scope, we want three success metrics: latency under 200ms p95 for clinician flows, end-to-end cost per consult under $0.20, and accuracy/regression tolerances under 3% compared to baseline. can Redwood instrument these?
[04:08] Diego: yes, we can instrument with per-route latency/cost breakdowns and run evals against prompt sets; we'll set up dashboards in Redwood Console and flag regressions via Redwood Optimize alerts.
[04:22] Marta: for the technical pilot, i've attached a sample trace and a 5k token workload — we'll share that after the call.
[04:28] Jordan: right, sending architecture diagram.
[04:30] Maya: great. next i want to go through the account heatmap — Samir, you lead and i'll annotate where Redwood can unblock.
[04:37] Samir: top priority is NorthStar Health Systems — big payer, long procurement. they need Private + dedicated nodes located in eu-west-1 and strict KMS. second tier is MercyClinics — faster close but mixed residency. third tier includes three mid-market hospital chains.
[04:55] Maya: ok, for NorthStar we should propose a pilot that runs on Dedicated w/ VPC in eu-west-1, include a 12-week pilot with explicit capacity commit and a rollback plan. we can offer a pilot discount and assign a Solutions Engineer for onboarding.
[05:09] Priya: i'll draft the onboarding checklist and add security docs required by NorthStar.
[05:15] Marta: question on data flow — will PHI ever touch Redwood-managed persistent storage?
[05:21] Diego: for Private deployments, storage can be customer-managed; for Dedicated we can offer data-at-rest encryption and short retention, but we can also enable customer-controlled retention policies so persistent storage is minimized.
[05:36] Jordan: also want clarity on who signs the DPA and what happens to logs post-contract.
[05:41] Maya: legal usually signs a DPA with a deletions clause and we can set a retention TTL for logs. we'll mark that as an action.
[05:47] Samir: any risks you foresee for the northstar deal from Redwood's side?
[05:51] Diego: operational risk is the initial network setup and routing rules for VPC peering — we should plan a pre-flight with Arcadia infra to validate peering, NAT, and egress rules. also model compatibility for the customer's chosen architecture (seq lengths, custom tokenizers) — bring a small validation harness.
[06:11] Jordan: good — i want an architecture validation step in the pilot plan.
[06:15] Maya: noted. last block is co-sell go-to-market enablement — marketing assets, one-pager, joint press?
[06:23] Samir: we'd prefer joint case study after pilot success, and a co-branded one-pager for sales kits. also a partner portal link for deal registration.
[06:33] Maya: we'll provide a co-sell kit and a reg process link.
[06:37] Priya: i'll include a pilot playbook and success metrics doc in the follow-up packet.
[06:42] Jordan: timeline check — we need pricing and SOC2 by 12/3 to get procurement moving; pilot kickoff early-to-mid Jan.
[06:51] Maya: that's doable. ok let's summarize real quick.
[06:55] Diego: recap from tech side: we will run the benchmark on Arcadia sample workloads (1k/5k/10k tokens) and deliver a spreadsheet; include Dedicated and Hosted variants and note p95 latency and token unit cost.
[07:06] Maya: business recap: we'll send co-sell one-pager with suggested financial split and pilot discount; partner ops will provide deal registration steps; Priya will prepare pilot onboarding checklist and retention/security notes.
[07:18] Jordan: action: i'll share architecture diagram, sample traces, and confirm security contact by Friday.
[07:23] Samir: we'll also identify the top 3 target accounts for joint AE outreach.
[07:27] Maya: perfect. any other questions?
[07:30] Marta: none from me.
[07:31] Jordan: no. thanks all.
[07:33] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with a packet. bye.

End of transcript.

Brief closing notes:

- Pilot success metrics agreed (latency p95 <200ms, cost per consult <$0.20, regression <3%).
- Expected pilot kickoff: early-mid January 2027 (post-procurement).
